findings.resolution: UNRESOLVED (open blocker). Before any execution, freeze 99-patient/five-fold membership independently of the schedule variable; require complete unique outer-join equality across candidate, A1 and A1_repeat over that frozen membership; reject missing/extra/duplicate members, duplicate folds and overlaps for any non-provisional verdict. Operator decision required; the executable was not modified, tested or approved here, and execution remains held. Only an independent APPROVE can close this finding.
findings.text: The proposed Sprint13B executable derives the verdict cohort size N_ALL from the editable driver variable FOLDS_TO_RUN rather than a frozen 99-patient/five-fold membership. The verdict gate requires len(g) == N_ALL before calling an arm 'better'/'worse', so a reduced FOLDS_TO_RUN (a subset of folds) shrinks N_ALL and still passes the 'all patients scored' gate, yielding a non-provisional verdict on fewer than 99 patients, contradicting the plan rule 'An arm is called better (or worse) only if its 98.75% interval against Sprint 12 A1 excludes 0 with all 99 patients scored.' The revised spec v2 proposes the correct fix (schedule-independent frozen 99/five-fold membership, complete unique candidate/A1/repeat joins, reject subsets/duplicates/overlaps) and explicitly states 'No code fixed/tested; execution hold', so the defect is preserved and corrected in proposal only; it is not resolved and remains an open blocker in the executable.

findings.resolution: UNRESOLVED (open blocker). Remove the magnitude-ratio gate; adopt the conjunctive screen rule and record distinct environment/repeat identities; do not treat one unseeded repeat as a variance estimate. Operator decision required; the executable was not changed, tested or approved, and execution is held. Only an independent APPROVE can close this finding.
findings.text: The proposed combined-results cell reports each primary arm's Dice difference as a multiple of a single retraining difference and the plan elevates this into an improvement criterion. The denominator is y = abs(mean A1_repeat-minus-A1 Dice change) from one unseeded retraining run; the code returns float('inf') when y==0 and inflates the ratio for small y, and takes the absolute value so a negative signed change is obscured. One unseeded retraining realization is a point estimate, not a variance estimate (train_seed is only a pairing label), so the ratio is neither a noise estimate nor a coherent gate. The revised spec v2 (answer 3 and review response) proposes removing the ratio/'not distinguishable from retraining' gate and adopting a conjunctive screen (both vs-A1 and vs-A1_repeat 98.75% intervals excluding zero in the same direction) with bound RNG/environment/repeat identities, labeled 'Proposal correction only; executable hold.' The defect is preserved and corrected in proposal only; it remains open in the executable.

findings.resolution: UNRESOLVED (suggestion). Bind a label-blind finite/validity support policy, coverage provenance and fallback/SD-floor/coverage reporting; keep uncovered output at zero with fixed scoring support. No patient-level coverage audit is authorized in this analysis-only lane; interpretation and any implementation remain held. Only an independent APPROVE can close this finding.
findings.text: The proposed coverage/validity handling uses an all-four-perfusion-maps-zero-after-nan_to_num test as a proxy for perfusion coverage before computing per-patient z-score/histogram statistics. This is only a proxy: a single-channel non-finite value can be coerced to a window-floor value and still enter the statistics, and genuinely zero tissue can be excluded, so the proxy does not establish true acquisition coverage and may bias the per-patient transforms. The revised spec v2 (answer 6) proposes binding valid finite support (authenticated acquisition coverage intersect brain intersect per-channel finite values) before replacement/clipping, disclosing genuine-zero exclusion, recording coverage provenance/counts/fallbacks, holding empty/constant-support arms for review, and explicitly authorizes no patient-level coverage audit in this analysis-only lane. Preserved and corrected in proposal only; impact untested. Carried as a suggestion, not a verdict blocker, but it must be bound before interpretation.

rationale: I read the authenticated originals before relying on them and independently re-verified both the spec's load-bearing numeric claims and all four carried findings. Numeric checks: Sprint12 nnU-Net (ccd74c0e...) L469 (median epoch 35.69 s, infarct-in-brain min 83%, upper-clipping medians ncct 10%/cbf 8%/cbv 6%/mtt 3%/tmax 12%/cta 10%), L545 (A100-80GB, 179 GB/12 CPU), L548 (8.5 min skip), L698 (A1 Dice 0.200, no-CTA 0.195, pnorm 0.203), L707 (CTA effect +0.005 [-0.007,+0.016]), L708 (normalization +0.003 [-0.015,+0.020]); Sprint12b (7ad63a2b...) L815 (+0.008 [+0.000,+0.015], 15 predictions/patient 5x3), L816 (5/5), L818 (lesion F1 +0.009 [-0.004,+0.026]), L820 (MET), L823 (47 exploratory), L842 (MTT +0.014 [+0.006,+0.021]); Sprint13A aggregates (e5cb1b3e...) L31 (P1 +0.003, 97.5% +0.001,+0.004), L32 (P2 +0.028, 95% +0.016,+0.041 and 97.5% +0.015,+0.042; lesion F1 -0.030 [-0.048,-0.015]), L35 (same-rule fusion +0.025 [+0.014,+0.038]), L69 (correlation 0.81, found-by-neither 0.671), L209 (probability-mask Dice 0.9187), L251 (tuning not an unbiased held-out evaluation, size unknown). The cost arithmetic reconciles exactly against the public-price evidence (0175d1c5...): A100-80GB $2.4984/h, composite $3.387168/h (+8 cores/64 GiB) and $4.50288/h (+12 cores/180 GiB), and 35.69 x 250 x 5 = 12.39 h; the spec correctly labels these as estimates versus the single smoke-derived measurement and states no spending is authorized. I note one minor presentational point: answer 7 cites P2 as '+0.028 (+0.015,+0.042)', which is the 97.5% Bonferroni interval (matching the P1 97.5% label in the same sentence), not the 95% interval; the value is a genuine source interval and is not misstated, so I did not raise it as a blocking finding. The item2 scope and withheld per-patient materials are confirmed in the limitations evidence (97f0dce4...): 13A is operator-run aggregates with executed r4 code absent, 13B is an unexecuted proposal. The revised spec answers all eight plan questions, flags the Sprint12b overlap with the correct same-exposed-patients qualification, costs each option with explicit rate/overhead/uncertainty assumptions and scientific model-call estimates, challenges scope (rejects immediate all-arm commitment and the L-size causal framing, defers pnormct/second windows, rejects unbiased-stacking language for 13A), preserves reserved-cohort and exploratory limitations, and reaches STOP FOR OPERATOR REVIEW with no execution authority and no patient/GPU/Modal/model-call/dispatch work. Its handling of the four carried findings is correct under the bound revision policy: each original finding is preserved, cited to evidence, and accompanied by a proposed correction or a retained limitation with an explicit execution hold, and the author does not claim closure ('Responses are not closure; only independent APPROVE closes findings'). The current finding status index shows the single finding record (ed4e52a7...) still open with disposition null. Because the four findings (three blockers, one suggestion) are verified, unresolved defects in the proposed executable and provenance, and because a proposed correction is not resolution (the executable was not fixed, tested or opposing-reviewed, and execution/environment receipts are absent), the decision cannot be APPROVE, which requires findings=[]. The defects are correctable within item2 analysis-only scope and the proposal is sound as a STOP-for-operator artifact, so termination (REJECT) is not warranted. The correct disposition is to carry all four findings forward and return to the author within the authorized revision allowance. The findings, not this rationale, carry the decision.
